title: Seed incorporation ledger for retained continuity queue slices

observed: The canonical M-RECONCILE-002 projection contains seven completed slices.
Repository commit search returned multiple later continuity-owned queue-update commits whose commit identities are not represented in the canonical completed_slices array.
The latest incorporation-lag queue update explicitly requires a commit-keyed incorporation ledger before canonical promotion.
inferred: The canonical queue is a current projection, not a complete event ledger.
Commit identity must be preserved independently of normalized semantic similarity because several retained slices can address adjacent provenance concerns without being interchangeable.
proposed: Use commit SHA as the primary ledger key and record path, normalized completed_slice, canonical match, classification, evidence strength, and supersession target.
Treat search-derived entries as bounded candidates until each commit diff and changed path are fetched directly.
superseded: The assumption that a semantic match to one canonical bullet is sufficient to prove incorporation of every related queue-update commit.
unresolved: The exhaustive count of continuity queue-update commits across all branches and history.
The exact incorporation classification of each search-derived candidate beyond the directly inspected incorporation-lag and collector slices.
The immutable provenance of M-004, M-005, and M-006.

memory_recovered: A provenance-preserving incorporation ledger must be event-keyed by immutable commit identity; semantic queue bullets are projections and cannot substitute for the retained event history.
evidence_strength: direct canonical snapshot plus one directly fetched queue-update diff, prior direct collector comparison, and bounded repository commit-search candidates
falsification_route: Fetch every candidate commit and changed path directly.
Normalize each completed_slice and compare it to the exact canonical queue blob.
Replace unresolved classifications only when immutable path and semantic evidence agree.
reversibility: Additive record only; revert this commit without altering source history.
